A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ASAP online 3D bin-packing work, with readable text, equations, figures and tables. v1 ends with references and has no appendix; v2 includes Appendices A.1–A.5. Renamed policies and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Sections III.B and V report original simulation results, including distribution-shift diagnostics, packing comparisons before and after adaptation, and component ablations.

after.justification: Sections 3.2 and 5 retain original packing experiments, while the appendices additionally report action-retention diagnostics, MCTS comparisons, sensitivity results and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Both retain two GAT policies, ACKTR, two-phase MAML-based training and online adaptation of only the selection policy. v1 already describes proposing top-K candidates in Section IV.B. Renaming pruning as proposal and initialization/finetuning as pre-training/post-training does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same four in-distribution and three out-of-distribution cuboid-item datasets in discrete and noise-augmented continuous environments. The added diagnostics and sensitivity experiments reuse this coverage rather than introducing new tasks or populations.

E2.justification: v2 adds MCTS as an Approx Optim reference in both main comparison tables. MCTS appeared in v1's motivation but was absent from Tables I–II. PCT, AR2L and the discrete-only GOPT packing comparisons remain, together with the same two ASAP ablation variants.

E3.justification: Main dataset sampling and training/adaptation budgets remain unchanged. v2 adds runtime metrics and proposal-size controls. The preliminary frequency experiment is now described using MCTS with resampled futures, whereas v1 specifies fixed-sequence greedy continuations at randomly selected timesteps. This revises the stated protocol without establishing that the retained frequency plots were regenerated.

E4.justification: v2 adds systematic proposal-size sensitivity tests beyond the existing full/no-decomposition variants, comparisons of MCTS-action retention by generic and ASAP policies, broader distribution-mismatch plots, and runtime breakdowns. Appendix Table 3 also quantifies the MCTS pruning check only summarized in v1. The original MAML and decomposition ablations remain.

E5.justification: Table 4 and Appendix A.4 newly disclose three random seeds, including three-seed baseline testing. v1 provides no corresponding run information. This is a reporting addition, not evidence of an increased run count; neither version supplies variability estimates or confidence intervals for the main packing results.

E6.justification: All 77 matched method–dataset–environment rows retain their utilization, packed-item counts and adaptation deltas. v2 nevertheless adds substantial results: MCTS reference scores, action-inclusion rates, alternative proposal-size scores and inference, training and adaptation timings. For example, discrete Default MCTS utilization of 85.9% is newly tabulated; it is not an improvement in a retained ASAP result.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a mathematical complexity argument claiming that reducing the MCTS branching factor changes O(k1^n) to O(k2^n), absent from v1. No theorem or proof is added. The existing packing objective and MAML updates are retained, with Algorithm 1 moved to the appendix.

C1.justification: The central claims remain improved cross-distribution generalization and rapid selection-only adaptation through a two-policy, meta-trained solver, demonstrated in discrete and continuous settings. The proposal terminology and explicit conjecture framing refine the exposition without changing the core contribution's scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking computational cost to simulator action generation and feasibility checking, and explaining why the second policy adds little overhead. Appendix A.5 discusses fixed top-k selection versus probability thresholds and interprets the sensitivity results as robustness. The earlier generalization and adaptation interpretations largely remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.4 supplies substantial previously absent implementation information: GAT depth, embedding and hidden sizes, episode length, EMS heuristics, candidate limits, hardware and baseline settings such as AR2L's alpha=1. Runtime information is also added. The abstract newly promises code and data upon acceptance, rather than documenting an existing release.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zhao et al.'s Learning Practically Feasible Policies for Online 3D Bin Packing and removes Coulom's MCTS reference while retaining Kocsis and Szepesvári. The related-work section also narrows its concluding contrast with prior methods to their lack of adaptation. The broader literature coverage remains stable.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, motivation and method receive extensive rewriting, including consistent proposal terminology and clearer separation of pre-training, post-training and online adaptation. Experimental discussion is regrouped, and a structured appendix accommodates detailed material, including the relocated MAML algorithm.

P2.justification: The document switches from two-column to single-column layout. Main tables are reorganized to place discrete and continuous results alongside each other, with new reference rows and timing columns. Figure 2 combines retained frequency curves with new retention plots; the dataset figure moves to the appendix, which adds diagnostic plots, timing charts and tables.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence for the central proposal/selection rationale through action-retention diagnostics and proposal-size sensitivity tests, while filling important implementation gaps in v1. Runtime measurements make the practical adaptation claim more assessable despite unchanged main packing scores. These gains are tempered by absent variability estimates and reporting inconsistencies, notably continuous GOPT timings in Table 5 despite its stated discrete-only scope. Nevertheless, the added validation and documentation provide a substantial net improvement.
